$comment: Generated by contracts/tools/bundle.py. Do not edit.
title: Bundle

CreateRun.title: CreateRun
CreateRun.description: Request body for POST /runs: run a pipeline version that already passed Gate A.

reuse_run_id.description: Reuse this run's results for every step whose definition is unchanged; run the rest (ADR-0026). Omitted: run from the start.

run_from_node_id.description: Run this step and every step after it again, even where unchanged; reuse or take from the cache only the steps before it (ADR-0026 amendment). It must be a step of the version. Omitted: only changed steps run.

AttemptOutput.title: AttemptOutput
AttemptOutput.description: One committed output of an attempt: the port that produced it and the artifact.

Problem.title: Problem
Problem.description: Error response body. Lists every problem found, not only the first.

TablePage.title: TablePage
TablePage.description: One page of rows from a tabular artifact, for display (GET /artifacts/{id}/rows). Cells are display text, cut to a bounded length; a missing cell is listed by column index and its text is empty. Wide tables return only their first columns.

offset.description: Index of the first row in this page.

total_columns.description: Columns in the table; more than `columns` holds when the table is too wide to page whole.

data_type.description: Arrow data type name, for display only.

missing.description: Indexes of columns whose value is missing in this row.

OperatorSource.title: OperatorSource
OperatorSource.description: Read-only source of a registered operator's entrypoint module, so every step's code can be read like a code step's. Served by GET /operators/{id}/source; the API reads only files inside the operator's plugin pack.

path.description: Relative to the pack's src/, e.g. sprisk_clean/impute.py. Never an absolute path.

digest.description: The operator's implementation digest: the code that runs, and the code shown, are the same.

LoadedTable.title: LoadedTable
LoadedTable.description: A table a flow loads (ADR-0038), as listed by GET /loaded_tables: the latest output of a source step. Tables with the same content are one entry. Derived from run history; not the Dataset entity of arch §4, which keeps that name.

name.description: The file name the source step reads, or the step's id when it reads no file.

run_id.description: The latest run of that version, whose source step loaded the table.

LoadedTableUse.description: A step that loads the table, in the latest run of its version that loaded it.

KeyMatches.title: KeyMatches
KeyMatches.description: How the rows a step reads match another table, per column both share (ADR-0059), computed by Python on all rows: structure, nothing fitted. Methodology rules read it to decide a join.

rows.description: Rows of the table the step reads.

keys.description: Each column both tables share, in the step's column order; at most 200.

column.description: Dataset text: a column name both tables have.

matched_rows.description: Rows of the step's table whose value finds a row of the other table. Missing values never match.

most_rows_per_key.description: The most rows of the other table that share one value: above 1, a join would copy rows.

ProfilePlan.title: ProfilePlan
ProfilePlan.description: The deterministic explanation of which Dataset Explore sections apply to one immutable table and question version. It selects views from stored profile facts and the question ledger; it contains no rows and makes no methodology decision.

question_version_id.description: The formal question whose declared task, target and bindings selected the sections. Absent for neutral data exploration.

sections.description: Applicable sections in the fixed display order. The UI renders only these sections and their supplied reason.

limitations.description: Fixed statements about the evidence bounds or scope. They are explanations, not findings.

ProfileScope.description: Which permitted rows the plan describes. Input is descriptive only; train is the scope for learned preparation and model-selection evidence.

reason.description: A fixed, deterministic template naming the profile fact or question-ledger field that made this view applicable.

SampledRowGroups.description: Which row groups a sampled profile read: `chosen` of the source's `of` row groups, picked with `seed`, so the same files give the same sample.

DatasetProfile.title: DatasetProfile
DatasetProfile.description: A descriptive profile of one table (GET /artifacts/{id}/profile, ADR-0038; GET /dataset_versions/{id}/profile, ADR-0067), computed by Python. Bounded: at most the first 200 columns and 1,000,000 rows, histograms of at most 20 bins or the 30 most common values, a missing-value map of at most 40 row bands, correlation of at most 30 columns. The AI planner never reads it. Methodology rules read it of a step's train rows, and only its structure (types, duplicates, values that fail to convert) of the rows before the split (ADR-0059).

total_rows.description: Rows in the whole table. Absent: not counted, because counting would read a registered CSV source to its end (ADR-0067); the table has more rows than profiled_rows.

profiled_rows.description: Rows the profile covers: all of them, or 1,000,000 of a larger table, from its first rows or from the row groups sampled_row_groups names.

sampled_row_groups.description: Set when a Parquet source larger than the sample was profiled on whole row groups chosen at random (ADR-0067). Absent: the profile covers the first rows, or all of them.

band_rows.description: Rows in each band of the missing-value map; the last band may hold fewer.

duplicate_rows.description: Profiled rows equal in every column to an earlier one.

rows_with_gap.description: Profiled rows with at least one gap: a missing cell, or blank text in a text column.

co_missing.description: The column pairs most often empty in the same rows (a missing cell or blank text), most rows first, at most 5. Pairs never empty together are left out.

label.description: How the columns relate to a label column, when one was asked for (GET /artifacts/{id}/profile?target=). Of every row, held-out rows included: for looking, never for choosing (rule 8). Absent when none was asked for or the table has no such column.

findings.description: What stands out in the profiled rows, most important first, as plain sentences built from the counts above (ADR-0065). Descriptive: a finding is never evidence for a decision.

TableShift.title: TableShift
TableShift.description: How a table's numeric columns differ from another's, such as a split's train rows from its test rows (GET /artifacts/{id}/shift?against=, ADR-0065). Computed by Python on all rows; descriptive, for looking: it never feeds a decision.

columns.description: Each numeric column both tables share, at most 30, largest shift first.

ks.description: Two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic: the largest gap between the two tables' cumulative shares.

lower.description: Lower edge of the shared bins.

upper.description: Upper edge of the shared bins.

counts.description: This table's values in 20 equal-width bins over both tables' range.

other_counts.description: The other table's values in the same bins.

ClassificationReport.title: ClassificationReport
ClassificationReport.description: A classifier's test-set metrics (sprisk.ml.evaluate 2.1.0). Labels are the target's class values as text. No feature values: a sampled row is named by its index in the test table, whose rows show through GET /artifacts/{id}/rows.

estimator.description: The estimator's class name, inside a cost cut-off when there is one.

cut_off.description: Only for a model that decides by costs (ADR-0053).

expected_cost.description: Mean cost per test row; only with cut_off.

per_class.description: One per class, in the confusion matrix's label order.

top_confusions.description: The off-diagonal confusion cells with any rows, largest first, at most 10.

error_margins.description: Absent when the model gives no scores or got no row wrong.

matrix.description: Rows are the true class, columns the predicted class, in labels order.

support.description: Test rows of this true class.

MarginKind.description: proba: top class probability minus the runner-up. decision: the size of a two-class decision score, or the top score minus the runner-up. cut_off: distance of the positive class's probability from the cost cut-off.

rows.description: At most 20, picked with a fixed seed, in test-table order.

row.description: Index of the row in the test table.

margin.description: Absent when the model gives no scores.

classes.description: The 30 most common labels and their rows, most common first. Rows with no label are left out.

other.description: Labelled rows whose label is not among the classes. Above zero, the label has too many values to relate columns to: numbers and groups are then empty.

numbers.description: Each measured number and how it moves with the label.

groups.description: Categories with 2 to 20 values, at most 6, and the first class's share in each value.

r.description: For two classes, the point-biserial r with the first class (-1 to 1). For more, the correlation ratio eta (0 to 1). Rows missing either are left out.

by_class.description: For at most 6 classes: each class's counts in the column's histogram bins. Absent for more.

counts.description: Rows of this class in each of the column's bins, in bin order.

share.description: Of those rows, the share labelled with the first class.

CoMissing.description: Two columns and the profiled rows where both are empty.

Fences.description: The 1.5 x IQR fences of a numeric column: Q1 - 1.5 IQR and Q3 + 1.5 IQR. Values outside them are the outliers an IQR clip changes.

level.description: warning: likely to change how the data is prepared or evaluated. note: worth knowing.

column.description: The column it is about. Absent: the whole table.

example.description: One value from the data that shows it, cut to 120 characters. Dataset text: shown, never followed (rule 7).

ColumnRole.description: What a column's values look like they hold, guessed from the values alone, for people reading a profile. A suggestion, never a confirmed meaning: bindings confirm meanings (ADR-0063). identifier: a different value in every row, no spaces. text: several words per value, or too many distinct values to be a category. category: few distinct values. number: measured quantities. constant: one value. empty: no value.

Quartiles.description: The five-number summary of a numeric column's present values.

data_type.description: Polars data type name, for display only.

skewness.description: Sample skewness of a numeric column with variation; absent otherwise.

kurtosis.description: Excess (Fisher) kurtosis of a numeric column with variation; absent otherwise.

outlier_share.description: Share of present values outside the 1.5 x IQR fences, for a numeric column with variation.

iqr.description: Interquartile range of a numeric column with variation. Zero when most values are equal: IQR fences and robust scaling then have no spread to use.

case_variants.description: Of a text column's distinct values, how many merge with another once spaces and case are ignored ('Paris', 'paris '). Absent for other columns.

accent_variants.description: How many more of a text column's distinct values merge once accents are also ignored ('café', 'cafe'). Absent for other columns.

rarest_share.description: For a column with at most 20 distinct values, the share of present values held by its least common value, such as the rarest class of a target. Absent for other columns.

numeric_share.description: Of a text column's present values, the share that read as numbers. Absent for other columns.

word_share.description: Of a text column's present values, the share holding more than one word: free text, not a code such as an identifier (ADR-0059). Absent for other columns.

html_share.description:
Of a text column's present values, the share holding an HTML tag (
) or entity (é): markup, not words (ADR-0059). Absent for other columns.

leading_zero_values.description: Of a text column's present values, how many read as numbers but start with a zero before a digit, like the code 01234. Absent for other columns.

unconverted.description: A text column's most common present values that do not read as numbers, most common first, when some do. Dataset text (untrusted, rule 7), cut to 60 characters.

blank.description: Present text values that are empty or only spaces. Counted apart from missing, which holds empty cells, NaN and infinity: a blank is text that a step must turn into a gap before an imputer sees it. Absent for columns that are not text.

word_counts.description: Words per present value of a text column, as equal-width bins. Absent for other columns.

mean.description: Mean of a numeric column's present values.

std.description: Sample standard deviation of a numeric column with variation.

outliers.description: Present values outside the fences, for a numeric column with variation.

missing_by_band.description: Share of gaps (0 to 1) in each row band, in row order: missing cells, and blank text in a text column.

histogram.description: Absent when every value is missing.

kind.description: bins: equal-width bins of a numeric column. top_values: the 30 most common values of any other column, most common first.

other.description: For top_values: present values not in any bar (the long tail). Absent for bins.

lower.description: For bins: the bin's lower edge. Absent for top values.

upper.description: For bins: the bin's upper edge. Absent for top values.

Correlation.description: Pearson correlation of numeric columns that vary (at most 30). Each pair uses the rows where both are present; a pair with fewer than 10 such rows, or with no variation on them, is left out.

rows.description: Rows where both columns are present.

FigureSet.title: FigureSet
FigureSet.description: Figures a step drew (ADR-0024), converted by the worker: matplotlib as SVG text, Plotly as its figure JSON text. GET /artifacts/{id}/figures returns the first ones from a figures or display report, without the tables a code step showed.

content.description: SVG markup, a Plotly figure as JSON text, or a Vega-Lite spec as JSON text (Altair).

CodeDisplay.title: CodeDisplay
CodeDisplay.description: What a code step showed (ADR-0020): printed text, tables and images, in order. Written by the worker as the step's display artifact; every part is capped.

table.description: Present for kind table: the first rows only.

figure.description: Present for kind figure: a plot the code drew, as SVG, Plotly or Vega-Lite (ADR-0024).

png_base64.description: Present for kind image: a PNG, base64-encoded. Written by older code steps; new ones write figures.

label.description: The code that was shown, as written: a name such as summary, or an expression such as df.head(). Absent for printed text, figures shown at the end, and older code steps.

line.description: The line of the step's code that showed it: a show() or display() call, or the last line. Absent when it was shown at the end of the run, or by older code steps.

channel.description: For printed text: which stream it came from. Absent for displayed values. Warnings arrive on stderr.

CodeInterface.title: CodeInterface
CodeInterface.description: What a code step's run found about its interface (ADR-0021): names it reads, literal settings it could expose, and values it ends with. Suggestions, not a claim that arbitrary code is understood.

files.description: Files the code reads (ADR-0025): inputs, never parameters. Omitted in reports written before ADR-0025.

reader.description: The call that reads it, e.g. read_csv or open.

bound.description: True when the name is provided by the step (its input table or a library); false means the code reads a name nothing defines.

default_text.description: The literal as written in the source.

effective_text.description: The literal the run used, as Python source.

origin.description: inferred until the user exposes it (confirmed).

type.description: Python type of the final value, e.g. polars.DataFrame.

chosen.description: This value became the step's data output.

fields.description: For tables: their columns with type and missing count, for the Data tab's variable explorer (ADR-0030). Capped.

sample.description: For tables: the first rows (ADR-0030). Omitted once the report's size budget is used up.

text.description: For other values: their repr, cut to a bounded length (ADR-0030).

CodeSplitRequest.title: CodeSplitRequest
CodeSplitRequest.description: Notebook cells to split into code steps (ADR-0031), in notebook order. Body of POST /code/split. Never executed.

together.description: Cells first..last (from 0) start as one step: the cells a person picked for Create node (ADR-0036). Absent: every cell starts alone.

CodeSplit.title: CodeSplit
CodeSplit.description: Code steps read from notebook cells (ADR-0031): each step's source, the cells it holds and the tables it reads and passes on, the links between steps, and notes for the person. A suggestion they confirm before a flow is made.

source.description: The step's code: its cells, with the imports and literals it uses from earlier cells copied in.

parameters.description: Top-level literals in the step's code, its own or copied in, that can be exposed as settings.

cells.description: Indexes (from 0) of the cells this step holds.

cell.description: Index (from 0) of the cell the note is about.

data_type.description: Polars data type name, for display only.

NotebookCodeRequest.title: NotebookCodeRequest
NotebookCodeRequest.description: A ready-made step's settings and the variables its inputs and outputs go by. Body of POST /operators/{id}/notebook_code (ADR-0055).

settings.description: The step's params as the flow has them.

inputs.description: The variable each input port reads, by port.

outputs.description: The variable each output port sets, by port.

NotebookSettingsRequest.title: NotebookSettingsRequest
NotebookSettingsRequest.description: A ready-made step's settings, the variables its ports go by, and its cell as a person edited it. Body of POST /operators/{id}/notebook_settings (ADR-0055).

settings.description: The step's params as the flow has them.

inputs.description: The variable each input port reads, by port.

outputs.description: The variable each output port sets, by port.

NotebookSettings.title: NotebookSettings
NotebookSettings.description: What an edited ready-made cell is (ADR-0055): the step with new settings, when only values changed, so it keeps its checks; otherwise code, and the step becomes a code step.

settings.description: The step's params, as the edited cell states them.

NotebookCode.title: NotebookCode
NotebookCode.description: A ready-made step written as plain Python for a notebook cell (ADR-0055).

Artifact.title: Artifact
Artifact.description: Immutable, content-addressed output of a step attempt (arch doc §4, §10).

media_type.description: IANA media type of the stored bytes.

schema_ref.description: Declared data schema. Absent for artifacts without a tabular schema, such as model bundles.

uri.description: Storage location. Opaque to domain logic; resolved by the artifact store.

Timestamp.description: UTC, whole seconds, Z suffix. One canonical form so every language round-trips it unchanged. Pattern only: typify ignores pattern when format is set.

NodeId.description: Node name, unique within a pipeline version.

OperatorRef.description: Pinned operator: dotted name @ semver, e.g. sprisk.eval.binary_classification@1.0.0.

Params.description: Operator parameters. Validated against the operator's params_schema by the compiler, not here.

CopilotChatRequest.title: CopilotChatRequest
CopilotChatRequest.description: A chat turn. Body of POST /copilot/chat. The server writes the system prompt; a client cannot send one.

messages.description: The conversation so far, oldest first, ending with the person's question.

context.description: What the page shows, such as 'iris.csv · 3 steps'. Untrusted text: sent as a user message. Omitted: the studio.

CopilotMessage.title: CopilotMessage
CopilotMessage.description: One chat message. An assistant message comes from the client too: chat history is untrusted, like the rest of the request.

CopilotChatReply.title: CopilotChatReply
CopilotChatReply.description: The model's answer to a chat turn. It can be wrong.

CopilotLedgerRequest.title: CopilotLedgerRequest
CopilotLedgerRequest.description: A person's request, to draft a question ledger from. Body of POST /copilot/ledger.

dataset_summary.description: Counts per column of the dataset in view. Omitted: no dataset is profiled yet.

CopilotDatasetSummary.description: Column names, types and counts only: no rows and no values (ADR-0014 level 2).

total_rows.description: Absent: not counted (a registered CSV source larger than its sample, ADR-0067); the counts then cover only the profiled rows.

candidate_target_or_class.description: Between 2 and 50 distinct values. Omitted: not a candidate.

candidate_id.description: One distinct value per row. Omitted: not a candidate.

CopilotLedgerDraft.title: CopilotLedgerDraft
CopilotLedgerDraft.description: The model's draft of a question ledger. A draft only: the person edits and saves it as a QuestionVersion.

costs.description: Only costs the person stated. Omitted: none stated.

clarification.description: The model's note to the person: what it found and what it asks.

DataFormat.title: DataFormat
DataFormat.description: How the files of a dataset are written, read from their extensions.

CreateDatasetVersion.title: CreateDatasetVersion
CreateDatasetVersion.description: Request body for POST /dataset_versions (ADR-0067): register data where it lives. Never a copy, never credentials.

location.description: An absolute local path, or a file://, s3://, gs:// or az:// URI, of one file or a folder of files. The API refuses other schemes and local paths outside the data roots.

DatasetVersion.title: DatasetVersion
DatasetVersion.description: Immutable reference to data where it lives (arch doc §3, ADR-0067): its location and a fingerprint of its files' metadata. sprisk never copies the data and never stores credentials. Changed data is a new version.

name.description: The last part of the location. Dataset text (untrusted, rule 7).

location.description: Where the data lives. A local path is kept as its canonical file:// URI.

size_bytes.description: Total bytes of the files. Exact in JavaScript up to 9 PB.

fingerprint.description: sha256 over each file's path, size, and e-tag or modified time, sorted by path. Metadata, not content: the bytes are never read to register.

SourceProfileRequest.title: SourceProfileRequest
SourceProfileRequest.description: What Rust sends the source profiler (python -m sprisk_profile.source, ADR-0067) on stdin: the files it listed and checked against the data roots, resolved through symlinks. Python reads only these, never a pattern.

target.description: The label column to relate the others to. Dataset text (untrusted, rule 7). Absent: no label.

files.description: At least one, in order: resolved local paths, or object-store URIs (s3://, gs://, az://) read with the credentials in the environment.

ExecutionPlan.title: ExecutionPlan
ExecutionPlan.description: A pipeline version as Rust compiled it (arch doc §9, ADR-0070): its steps in run order, each with its resolved ports. Gate B builds its graph from this, never from the manifests. Carries only what Gate B reads today.

steps.description: At least one, in run order.

inputs.description: Each connected input, by port name.

outputs.description: Every output port, a code step's named ones included (ADR-0031).

rows_from.description: The input ports whose rows this output holds: every input, except that a fits_on_train step's train outputs hold only its train input (ADR-0018).

Method.title: Method
Method.description: A method's method.yaml (ADR-0063): the decision it owns, what it needs, its options and what each option promises. Its method.py holds decide() and one verify_<name>() per verification.

name.description: The decision's professional name, for titles ("Duplicate analysis"); `question` explains it. A rule's `name` means the same.

activity.description: The group this decision is shown in: one stage card on the canvas, one notebook section.

question.description: The decision as a question for people.

pitfall.description: What goes wrong for the analysis when this decision is made badly, for people.

compare.description: Its decide() answers with a shortlist, not one option: the engine compares those options on the same folds and takes the winner by ADR-0050 (one-standard-error rule, baseline test). Each option replaces one step. Absent: false.

changes.description: The kinds of model input its step changes, each a lane in the data flow; a step changing two kinds is where those lanes meet. Absent: its step works on the whole table, or it adds no step.

verifications.description: Promises an option can make, by name. An option lists the ones it makes in verify.

source.description: The published standard the method follows.

DecisionKey.description: <area>.<decision>, the key other methods read a decision by.

ConceptId.description: <pack>.<concept>, a meaning defined in a pack's concepts.yaml.

EvidenceKind.description: <area>.<evidence>, a measured fact one operator produces.

MethodAppliesWhen.description: When the method applies. Absent: always.

assets.description: Kinds of file the question must bind to its rows (QuestionVersion.asset_bindings), every one. Absent: none needed.

MethodNeeds.description: Everything decide() may read. It reads nothing else.

statements.description: The question statements decide() may read (ADR-0063 slice 6). Absent: none.

QuestionStatement.description: A statement a person makes on the question, never guessed: what each mistake costs, how far a person must follow a prediction, the score that is good enough.

MethodStatements.description: Each needed statement the question makes. Left out: not stated.

description.description: What choosing this option does to the data or the flow, for people.

condition.description: When the method picks this option, as a short formula for a flowchart branch, e.g. |skew| > 1 or classes = 2 ∧ costs stated. `when` says it in words.

when.description: In a few words, when the method picks this option, e.g. the column is skewed.

rationale.description: Why this option is right then, for people.

verify.description: The verifications this option promises, by name.

MethodAction.description: What the option changes. Absent: nothing.

MethodStop.description: The walk stops once this option is taken (ADR-0063 slice 6), with the method's reason as its detail. limitation: a limit the walk cannot go past, such as no lift over the baseline. uncovered: a change the walk cannot make yet, such as reopening the features.

MethodLimits.description: Fixed counts the method decides by, by name, such as the most looks at the folds (ADR-0063 slice 6); not a step's settings. decide() reads them; the engine reads one it enforces itself. Absent: none.

MethodSet.description: Sets settings on the step with this role, keeping its operator and its other settings (ADR-0063 slice 6).

settings.description: Settings that do not depend on the project. Absent: none.

from_statements.description: Settings read from a statement the method needs: setting name to statement. A statement the question does not make leaves its setting out. Absent: none.

MethodInsert.description: Inserts a step running operator on the rows the step with role `before` reads (ADR-0063 slice 6).

node_id.description: The inserted step's id; a free one with a suffix when the flow already has it.

settings.description: Params that do not depend on the project. Absent: none.

from_evidence.description: Params read from a field of evidence the method needs: param name to <area>.<evidence>.<field>. Absent: none.

concepts.description: Params a project's binding fills: param name to concept. Absent: none.

MethodBind.description: Binds a concept to a column that the producer of an evidence kind adds.

column.description: A column the producer writes, never a dataset column.

promise.description: What holds when it passes, for people.

MethodRequest.title: MethodRequest
MethodRequest.description: Rust to the method session (`python -m sprisk_workers.method`), one JSON line per decision (ADR-0063): the method module Rust picked from the loaded catalog, and only what its needs declare. decide() may read nothing else.

module.description: Path of the method's method.py, from the catalog Rust loaded; never from a client. A local path, so this message is only for the method process on the same machine, never stored.

options.description: The ids of the method's options: decide() chooses or asks for one of them.

evidence.description: Each needed kind that was measured. A needed kind left out cannot be measured, because its producer reads a concept no binding names.

decisions.description: Each needed decision, by its key: the option chosen.

bound.description: The needed concepts a stated, confirmed or method-made binding names. Never a column name.

ruled_out.description: Options this walk took whose promise then failed, so the decision is made again: they are left out of `options`. Absent: none.

statements.description: The needed statements the question makes. Absent: the method needs none.

limits.description: The method's limits. Absent: it has none.

RuledOutOption.title: RuledOutOption
RuledOutOption.description: An option a failed promise rules out for the rest of a walk (ADR-0063 amendment): the verification that failed and what its check found.

VerificationRequest.title: VerificationRequest
VerificationRequest.description: Rust to the method session, one JSON line per promise to check (ADR-0063): the method module Rust picked from the loaded catalog, the verification's name, the fields of the one evidence kind it needs, as the step's producer measured them, and its settings. verify_<name>() may read nothing else.

module.description: Path of the method's method.py, from the catalog Rust loaded; never from a client. A local path, so this message is only for the method process on the same machine, never stored.

evidence.description: The fields of the evidence kind the verification needs.

settings.description: The verification's settings from method.yaml; empty when it has none.

MethodFiles.title: MethodFiles
MethodFiles.description: Read-only files of one method folder (ADR-0063): its method.yaml and method.py, as the packs loaded them, so a person sees the code that decides and checks a step. Served by GET /methods/{id}/source; the API reads only files inside the method's folder.

path.description: Relative to the method folder, e.g. method.yaml. Never an absolute path.

VerificationName.description: A verification a method declares, the name of its verify_<name>() function.

MethodAssurance.description: How a method's option was taken: confirmed, a person answered the method's ask; rule, the method chose it unasked.

MethodAnswer.title: MethodAnswer
MethodAnswer.description: The method session's one JSON line per request, tagged by `answer`: what decide() returned, what verify_<name>() found, or why the method refused its request. Any other failure ends the session.

outcome.description: choose: the method applies the option. ask: a person confirms the option, or picks another, before anything relies on it.

reason.description: Why, for a person. For ask, the question itself.

MethodShortlisted.description: A compared method's decide() (`compare: true`, ADR-0063 D3): the options worth comparing. The engine compares them on the same folds and takes the winner; decide() never picks it.

shortlist.description: Two or more of the method's options, in its own order: a comparison needs something to compare.

reason.description: Why these options, and why any other was left out, for a person.

error.description: The method's own error (an undeclared read, an unknown option). It may name local paths, so it goes to the log, not to a client.

detail.description: What the evidence showed, for a person.

VerificationOutcome.description: What verify_<name>() found. pass: the promise holds. fail: it does not. inconclusive: the evidence cannot say, such as one side with no groups. Never stale: only the control plane knows what changed since.

DecisionAnswer.description: A person's answer to a method's ask (ADR-0063 amendment): the option to apply for the decision. The walk applies it with assurance confirmed.

ConceptSet.title: ConceptSet
ConceptSet.description: A pack's concepts.yaml (ADR-0063): the meanings its methods and operators may ask for. Served by GET /concepts with the concepts of every loaded pack.

ConceptKind.description: label: what a model predicts; an all-rows step may never read it. text: free text. entity_identifier: groups rows of one real-world thing. time: when a row's event happened.

BindingSourceKind.description: column: a column of the loaded data. derived: a column a step adds.

Binding.title: Binding
Binding.description: Which column means a concept in one project (ADR-0063). Column names live only here.

step.description: The step that adds the column. Absent: a column of the loaded data.

OperatorRole.description: The one job a step does in a flow, so methods place and replace steps by role, and the engine builds a step of a role from its default operator, never by name (ADR-0064). score: scores a model on rows. score_shares: compares the class shares of train and test at the final score. cross_validate: scores a candidate on folds. select: chooses among compared candidates. row_filter: only drops rows.

SplitFolds.description: How a split's folds are made when models are compared on its train rows (ADR-0064). plain: shuffled rows. group: whole values of the split's group_column. time: in order of the split's time_column, never reshuffled.

OperatorAttach.description: Where the engine adds an evidence producer: on the rows going into (input) or coming out of (output) the step with this role.

OperatorScope.description: all: reads every row, before the split, so it may never read a label concept. train: reads train rows only.

default.description: The producer the engine adds when several operators produce this kind. Absent: false.

EvidenceSet.title: EvidenceSet
EvidenceSet.description: What one evidence producer measured, written to its output port named evidence (ADR-0063): each kind it produces, with each field's value. The operator's produces says which kinds and fields, of which types; the control plane checks the file against it when the step's outputs are saved.

EvidenceValue.description: A field's value: a number, a yes or no, a short text, or a list of short texts (string_list).

EvidenceFieldType.description: string_list: short values shown to people, such as the ids of overlapping groups.

MethodReplace.description: Replaces the step with this role by a step running operator.

settings.description: Params that do not depend on the project. Absent: none.

concepts.description: Params a project's binding fills: param name to concept. A param the operator already maps to a concept is not listed here. Absent: none.

BindingSetBy.description: Who set the binding, tagged by assurance: a person stated it, or a method's option made it, confirmed by a person or set unasked by the method (rule).

MethodologyStage.description: Stages in decision order (ADR-0059): the split comes before cleaning, since cleaning rules measure train rows.

MethodologyRule.title: MethodologyRule
MethodologyRule.description: The declarative manifest of one methodology rule package (ADR-0042), loaded from methodology/<pack>/rules/<rule>/rule.yaml. Served read-only by GET /methodology_rules.

status.description: draft: a decision not built yet, never run; its condition and observes are notes. active: a method shown on the map in its own words (ADR-0063 slice 6); a rule.yaml is always a draft.

reads.description: Facts this active rule may read, by name from the fact catalog, e.g. question.target or column.*.kurtosis; * stands for a column or setting name. Rust sends only these (ADR-0045).

question.description: The decision as a person asks it, e.g. How should missing values be filled? Shown on the Methodology page; nothing that decides reads it. Required on an active rule (ADR-0045 amendment).

decides.description: The one decision this rule owns; unique across loaded packs.

observes.description: Design notes on a draft rule's inputs; an active rule declares reads instead.

policy_thresholds.description: Default thresholds the rule decides with.

alternatives.description: The options, as people read them.

condition.description: A draft rule's design note on when this applies.

when.description: In a few words, when the rule takes this route, e.g. the column is skewed. For people; nothing that decides reads it (ADR-0045 amendment).

settings_schema.description: JSON Schema for this alternative's settings.

operator.description: Operator the action builds; may name one not yet registered.

node_id.description: insert_step: the id of the step it adds, saying what the step is about (ADR-0057).

params.description: Operator params; '{settings.x}' strings are filled from the alternative's settings.

MethodologyRuleSource.title: MethodologyRuleSource
MethodologyRuleSource.description: Read-only files of one draft rule: its manifest. Served by GET /methodology_rules/{id}/source; the API reads only files inside the rule's folder.

path.description: Relative to the rule folder, e.g. rule.yaml. Never an absolute path.

RuleActionType.description: What choosing an alternative does to the flow. Rust builds graph effects for replace_node, remove_node (ADR-0043) and insert_step before the rule's step (ADR-0057); reopen changes nothing in the flow: it names the stage its params give (ADR-0059). The others describe actions not wired yet. A new type is a contract change, so a typo cannot pass as a silent no-op.

GraphEffect.description: Typed mutation previewed and compiled before it can create a pipeline version.

oneOf.description: Removes the step and feeds each of its outputs from its input of the same name (ADR-0043).
Adds step node_id before step `before`, on the train and test rows `before` learns from (ADR-0057).

other.description: A step that joins: the output feeding its `other` input, a source table no step read before (ADR-0059). Absent for a step with one input.

oneOf.description: Adds step node_id beside the flow: each of its inputs reads the output named in inputs, and no step reads it yet, such as an evidence producer (ADR-0063).
Feeds input port of step node_id from output from instead of what fed it (ADR-0063).

DecisionProposal.title: DecisionProposal
DecisionProposal.description: Immutable resolver output. It explains alternatives and previews typed effects; it does not mutate a graph.

rule.description: The compared method whose options it offers a person (ADR-0063 D3); a rule's id in proposals made before slice 6.

shortlist.description: The options worth comparing, as the compared method shortlisted them (ADR-0044, ADR-0063 D3).

MethodologyDecision.title: MethodologyDecision
MethodologyDecision.description: Immutable record of one decision made through Apply: a rule's alternative, or a method's option (ADR-0064).

MethodologyDecisionByRule.title: MethodologyDecisionByRule
MethodologyDecisionByRule.description: A rule's alternative atomically applied to a new pipeline version.

selection_id.description: The SelectionDecision this choice followed or overrode (ADR-0050). Absent when no comparison had decided.

missed_guardrails.description: The guardrails the chosen alternative failed in the SelectionDecision this choice overrode, with its values (ADR-0052). Absent when it failed none.

test_rows_seen_by.description: Earlier versions applied from the same proposal whose runs had already scored the test rows (arch doc §11). Absent when none had.

MethodologyDecisionByMethod.title: MethodologyDecisionByMethod
MethodologyDecisionByMethod.description: A method's option taken through the same Apply as a rule's (ADR-0064): keyed per walk round, refused on a changed base, and cited by every step it changed.

pipeline_version_id.description: The version the option made. Absent when it changed no step.

effects.description: The patch the option applied, in order. Absent: it changed no step.

selection_id.description: The SelectionDecision a compared method's option won by (ADR-0063 D3, ADR-0050). Absent for any other method.

bindings.description: The bindings the option made. Absent: none.

promises.description: The verifications the option promises, by name. Absent: none.

evidence.description: What the method read, whether it chose or a person answered. Absent: it read none.

ModelSelection.title: ModelSelection
ModelSelection.description: How Sprisk is choosing one step of a flow's model pipeline (ADR-0050): a model step's shortlist proposal, or a preparation step's proposal; the version that cross-validates it; and that version's latest run. Its select step's output is the SelectionDecision.

MethodologyCheck.title: MethodologyCheck
MethodologyCheck.description: Result of one Gate B methodology rule on one pipeline version (arch doc §4, §8). Immutable; re-checking creates a new record.

cited_nodes.description: Nodes the verdict is about. Empty when the rule found nothing to inspect.

limitations.description: What the rule could not assess. Omitted when there is nothing to say.

NotebookVersion.title: NotebookVersion
NotebookVersion.description: One saved state of a notebook (ADR-0036): its ordered code and Markdown cells. Immutable; each save is a new version. Outputs are not saved: they belong to the session.

parent_id.description: Version this one was saved over. Absent for a notebook's first version.

pipeline_version_id.description: The flow version this notebook was made in or last synced into (ADR-0037). The notebook belongs to that flow and its later versions. Absent: not in a flow yet.

removed.description: Present and true: the notebook was deleted in this version (ADR-0041). It is no longer listed; its history stays readable. Absent otherwise.

NotebookCellId.description: Stable within a notebook across versions, as in Jupyter's nbformat 4.5.

NotebookExecute.title: NotebookExecute
NotebookExecute.description: Run one cell's code in the notebook's session kernel (ADR-0036). Body of POST /notebooks/{id}/execute.

NotebookExecution.title: NotebookExecution
NotebookExecution.description: What one cell did in the session kernel: its execution count, what it printed and showed (capped, as a code step's display), and its error. Scratch, not provenance (ADR-0036).

execution_count.description: The kernel's count for this execution. Absent when the cell never got one (timed out before it started).

error.description: Present when status is error or interrupted.

kernel_restarted.description: Present and true when the kernel restarted before or during this cell (memory cap, crash, stuck interrupt): every variable is gone. Absent otherwise.

NotebookExecutionEvent.title: NotebookExecutionEvent
NotebookExecutionEvent.description: One line of a cell's execution as it happens (ADR-0041), from the session host to Rust and, when asked with Accept: application/x-ndjson, from POST /notebooks/{id}/execute to the browser. Tagged by `kind`: `running` lines carry every output so far; the last line is `done`, or `failed` when the kernel stopped answering after the stream began (earlier failures are an HTTP error).

execution_count.description: The kernel's count for this execution, once it has one.

outputs.description: Every output so far, not only the new ones, capped as in the result.

traceback.description: Plain text lines, colour codes removed.

NotebookVariables.title: NotebookVariables
NotebookVariables.description: Which names the session kernel holds and whether each is a table, so Create node can refuse an output that cannot cross a boundary (ADR-0036).

type.description: Module and class, e.g. pandas.DataFrame. Absent when not defined.

table.description: A pandas or polars DataFrame: the one kind of value that crosses a node boundary today.

NotebookKernelRequest.title: NotebookKernelRequest
NotebookKernelRequest.description: Rust to the session host, one JSON line each (ADR-0036). Tagged by `op`. The host answers execute with NotebookExecutionEvent lines ending in `done` (ADR-0041) and variables with NotebookVariables; interrupt and shutdown get no answer.

Operator.title: Operator
Operator.description: Registered, versioned capability that a pipeline node runs (arch doc §5, §6).

title.description: The step's name for people: the standard term for what it does (Group split, Imputation). Shown by the UI, CLI and notebooks; the description explains it in plain words. Absent: the operator's name stands in.

notebook_code.description: Python `module:function` that writes this step as plain Python for a notebook cell, with its settings and names filled in (ADR-0055). A test runs that code against the step on fixtures. Absent: the step has no plain code yet.

fits_on_train.description: True for a step that reads train and test on ports of those names, fits on train only and writes each from its own rows. Such a step keeps train rows apart, and is refit on each fold when models are compared (ADR-0050). Absent: it may mix rows.

stage.description: The stage a step of this operator is in, unless its node says another (ADR-0055). Absent: the UI shows it with other steps.

role.description: The job the step does, for methods that replace a step by role (ADR-0063). Absent: no method places it by role.

role_default.description: True for the operator the engine uses when it builds a step of this role (ADR-0064). At most one per role. Absent: not a default.

folds.description: Set on a split: how its folds are made when models are compared. Absent: a flow with this split cannot be compared.

attach.description: Set on an evidence producer: where the engine adds it (ADR-0063).

scope.description: Which rows the step reads. Absent: whatever its inputs carry.

concepts.description: Params a project's binding fills: param name to concept (ADR-0063). Absent: none.

produces.description: The evidence the step measures, by kind, with its fields (ADR-0063). The step writes it as one EvidenceSet to its output named evidence, and needs an attach. Absent: none.

params_schema.description: JSON Schema for this operator's params. The compiler validates node params against it.

OperatorModel.description: Set on every operator that fits a model on rows, for preparation rules: how its fit reacts to its inputs. A model fits only the model; Clean steps prepare its inputs (ADR-0056).

family.description: Left out for a model that ignores its features, such as a dummy baseline.

tasks.description: The supervised tasks the model fits, so a shortlist rule can offer it (ADR-0044).

complexity.description: How flexible the model is, for the one-SE rule (ADR-0050): of the models within one standard error of the best, the one with the lowest complexity is recommended. 0 ignores its features; linear models are 1; tree ensembles 2. Set on every supervised model.

estimator.description: Python `module:function` returning the model unfitted, given its params except target, features and costs, so cross-validation can refit it per fold (ADR-0044, ADR-0046). Set on every supervised model.

search.description: The settings a study may tune, in this order, each with the values it tries (ADR-0052). Left out for a model with nothing to tune.

SearchSetting.description: One setting a study may tune: a params property of the model, and the finite list of values it tries. The registry checks each value against the property's schema.

ModelFamily.description: How a model operator's fit reacts to its inputs, for preparation rules: tree_ensemble splits on rank order; linear and distance_based depend on scale and outliers; density_based depends on scale and marks isolated rows as noise.

optional.description: An input the step may run without (ADR-0058): left unconnected, the step gets nothing for it. Only a matrix input may be optional today; the registry refuses any other.

PortKind.description: What a port carries. A table is Parquet; a matrix is rows by named number columns, stored sparse (SciPy CSR in .npz, ADR-0058): row i is row i of the table it was made from.

Effects.description: pure: same inputs give same outputs, cacheable. nondeterministic: not replayable. side_effecting: changes the outside world; never auto-retried.

PipelineVersion.title: PipelineVersion
PipelineVersion.description: Immutable typed graph of pinned operators (arch doc §4, §5). Structural checks (at least one node, unique node ids, known ports, no cycles) belong to the Rust compiler, not this schema.

question_version_id.description: Exact immutable question-ledger revision this flow answers. Absent only for legacy or not-yet-scoped flows.

parent_id.description: Version this one was derived from. Absent for the first version.

compares.description: The shortlist proposal whose models this version cross-validates (ADR-0046). A comparison is a side version, not an edit: it has no parent_id, so the proposal stays applicable. Absent on every other version.

compares_method.description: The compared method whose shortlist this version cross-validates (ADR-0063 D3), a side version like one that `compares` a proposal. A version has at most one of the two. Absent on every other version.

methodology_decision_id.description: Decision that produced this node state. Absent for a hand-authored node.

code.description: This step's own code in this version, replacing its operator's implementation (ADR-0028). Omitted: the operator's code runs.

from_notebook.description: The notebook cells this node was created from (ADR-0036). Omitted: not made from a notebook.

title.description: The kind of step, as people read it: Box plot, Train/test split (ADR-0055). The step's id says what it is about. Omitted: its operator's name.

stage.description: The stage notebook this step's cell is in (ADR-0055). Omitted: the stage its operator implies.

notes.description: Markdown cells shown with this step's cell (ADR-0055). Omitted: none.

names.description: The variable each output port goes by in the notebook, by port (ADR-0055). Omitted: the port names.

Stage.description: A flow's stages in working order; each is one notebook (ADR-0055, ADR-0065). Load reads the data, Explore looks at all of it, Clean fixes what needs no fitting, Split sets the test rows aside.

before.description: Markdown cells above the step's cell, in order.

after.description: Markdown cells below it; only the last step of a stage has them.

VariableName.description: A Python name a cell sets or reads.

notebook_id.description: The notebook these cells belong to, so saving it again rebuilds its steps (ADR-0037). Absent on nodes made before.

function.description: The function in source that is the step.

QuestionVersion.title: QuestionVersion
QuestionVersion.description: Immutable formal statement of what an investigation asks (arch doc §4, §7). Every field records its origin. An absent target means no supervised target exists; never invent one.

parent_id.description: Version this one revises. Absent for the first version.

target.description: Target column. Absent when there is no legitimate supervised target.

entity_column.description: Column whose values identify the unit or group that must not cross an entity-aware split.

prediction_horizon.description: How far after prediction time the outcome is observed, preferably an ISO-8601 duration such as P30D.

costs.description: What each wrong prediction costs, for a two-class classification question (ADR-0053). Only a person can state it. Absent: unknown, so both mistakes are treated as costing the same.

interpretability.description: How far a person must follow each prediction, a hard constraint (ref-v3 0.4). high: only models a person can read, such as linear ones. Only a person can state it. Absent: not stated.

success_bar.description: The cross-validated score that counts as good enough, in a metric models are compared by (ADR-0059). Only a person can state it. Absent: not stated; the text acceptance criteria hold everything else.

bindings.description: Which column means each concept the packs ask for, in this project (ADR-0063). One binding per concept. Absent: none stated.

asset_bindings.description: Explicitly declared external assets linked to rows. Asset roots are never inferred or scanned implicitly.

answers.description: A person's answers to the methods' asks, one per decision key (ADR-0063 amendment). Absent: none given.

file_pattern.description: How a row's file is named from its columns, e.g. image_{imageid}_product_{productid}.jpg. Absent: link_column holds the file name, relative to asset_root.

origin.description: A bar is never inferred or measured: one set from the scores always looks met.

score.description: At least this for balanced_accuracy, at most this for expected_cost and rmse. The API refuses a balanced accuracy outside 0 to 1 and a negative cost or error.

origin.description: A constraint is never inferred or measured.

Interpretability.description: How far a person must follow each prediction. high: only models a person can read, such as linear ones.

Origin.description: explicit: user stated it. inferred: AI or rule guessed it. measured: computed from data. confirmed: user approved an inferred value.

origin.description: Costs are never inferred or measured.

positive.description: The class whose miss costs, as text.

false_negative.description: Cost of predicting another class for a `positive` row. Positive; the API refuses others.

false_positive.description: Cost of predicting `positive` for another row. Positive; the API refuses others. A correct prediction costs nothing.

blocks.description: Earliest stage this unknown must be resolved before.

Report.title: Report
Report.description: What a completed walk found, built from its records, never written by a model (ADR-0064). Immutable; one per completed walk. Its answer is the model's score on the test rows, scored once, against the success bar and the baseline.

question.description: The question's objective, as a person stated it.

claims.description: One per decision the walk made and per promise it checked, in trail order.

limitations.description: What the answer does not show.

evidence.description: The records the statement rests on. The engine builds every claim on at least one.

ReportEvidence.description: One record a claim rests on, by id.

Run.title: Run
Run.description: One execution of a pipeline version against its inputs (arch doc §4, §9). Status is the transactionally maintained current state; history lives in attempts and audit events.

reuse_run_id.description: The run whose unchanged results this run reused (ADR-0026). Omitted when it ran from the start.

run_from_node_id.description: The step this run ran again from, with every step after it (ADR-0026 amendment). Omitted when only changed steps ran.

finished_at.description: Set once the run reaches a terminal status.

Attempt.title: Attempt
Attempt.description: One try of one step (a node in a run). Retries create a new attempt with the next number; old attempts are never replaced (arch doc §9).

number.description: 1 for the first try of this step.

error.description: Set when state is failed or timed_out.

SelectionDecision.title: SelectionDecision
SelectionDecision.description: Which compared alternative cross-validation chose, and why (arch doc §11, ADR-0044, ADR-0050): a shortlisted model, or one way of doing a preparation step. The output of a select step: immutable, like every artifact. An alternative wins only by beating the baseline on the same folds; a reference baseline wins when none does.

folds.description: Number of cross-validation folds every candidate was scored on.

repeats.description: How many times the rows were shuffled into folds (ADR-0050). Absent: once, as before repeated folds.

seed.description: Seed that shuffled the rows into folds.

baseline.description: The candidate every other must beat. As a floor, a model that ignores its features; as a reference, the rule's recommended preparation.

baseline_role.description: Absent: floor, as decided before ADR-0050 compared preparation.

winner.description: The chosen candidate. Absent: no model beats a floor baseline. A reference baseline is the winner when no alternative beats it.

not_compared.description: Alternatives the comparison did not score, each with why (ADR-0050). Absent: decided before ADR-0050 recorded them.

limitations.description: What the comparison did not cover.

guardrails.description: Constraints a candidate had to meet to win, declared with the study (EXP-02, ADR-0052). Absent: none were declared.

positive_share.description: With costs: the share of the costed class in the train rows. Expected cost and each tuned cut-off hold at this share only (ADR-0053).

earlier_looks.description: Earlier comparisons of the same version and step, started on the same folds before this one, whether or not they finished (ADR-0052). Absent: none.

SelectionMetric.description: Fixed before any score is seen: balanced_accuracy (higher is better) for classification, expected_cost per row (lower is better) when the model step states costs (ADR-0053), rmse (lower is better) for regression. weighted_f1 (higher is better; F1 per class weighted by its share of rows) for classification when a person states it with the success bar (ADR-0059).

BaselineRole.description: What the baseline is for. floor: a model that ignores its features; it never wins, so no winner means no model beats it. reference: the rule's recommendation; it stands unless another alternative beats it (ADR-0050).

NotCompared.description: An alternative the comparison could not score on the folds, and why (ADR-0050).

reason.description: Why it was not scored on the folds.

fold_scores.description: The metric on each fold's validation rows, in fold order, repeat after repeat.

spread.description: Standard deviation of the fold scores.

search.description: How its settings were tuned (ADR-0052). Absent: it ran at the flow's settings.

guardrails.description: Each declared guardrail, in declared order, as this candidate met it. Absent: none were declared.

CandidateSearch.description: A tuned candidate: on each outer fold, the trial with the best inner score on that fold's training rows gave the fold score, so the fold scores describe the tuning, not one setting. `settings` is the trial with the best inner score on all train rows: the one to apply.

inner_mean.description: Mean inner score over the outer folds: what the search saw. Not a performance estimate.

chosen_in.description: How many outer folds chose this trial.

mean.description: Mean over the outer folds of the recall of `label`.

corrected_se.description: Its standard error, corrected for folds that share train rows as for the scores.

mean_difference.description: Mean fold-by-fold improvement over the baseline on the same folds; positive is better for either metric.

corrected_se.description: Standard error of that mean, corrected for folds that share train rows: the correction of Nadeau & Bengio (2003), applied to k-fold as in Bouckaert & Frank (2004).

p_value.description: One-sided p of the corrected repeated k-fold t-test that the alternative is no better than the baseline (Bouckaert & Frank 2004). Absent: decided by the one-SE screen, before ADR-0050's test.

beats_baseline.description: With p_value: whether the test rejects at α = 0.05 after a Holm adjustment over the other alternatives. Without: whether mean_difference is larger than one corrected_se, a screening rule.

Study.title: Study
Study.description: A comparison of a flow's model step with search trials and a budget (arch doc §11, ADR-0052). Its trials are the cross-validate steps of its comparison version; status is the transactionally maintained current state, like a run's.

pipeline_version_id.description: The flow version whose model step is studied.

proposal_id.description: The study's own shortlist proposal; its comparison is the study's.

comparison_id.description: The comparison version holding the trials and the select step.

seed.description: Shuffles the grid for random search.

max_trials.description: Most trials the study may hold; checked when it is built.

max_wall_seconds.description: Longest the study's run may take, counted from its start.

guardrails.description: Declared when the study is created, before this study's scores exist (EXP-02). Earlier comparisons of the same step may have been seen; the decision lists them (ADR-0052).

deadline.description: When the budget runs out: the scheduler leases no step after it. Absent until the run starts.

finished_at.description: Set once the study reaches a terminal status.

StudyStrategy.description: grid: every combination of the manifest's values. random: a seeded sample of them, without replacement (ADR-0052).

StudyStatus.description: running: its run has not ended. completed: the select step decided. budget_reached: the wall-time budget ran out; finished trials are kept and nothing is decided. failed: a step failed after its retries.

Guardrail.description: A constraint a candidate must meet to win (EXP-02). recall: the mean over outer folds of the recall of `label` must be at least `at_least`.

CreateStudy.title: CreateStudy
CreateStudy.description: Request to study a model step (ADR-0052). Settings and their values come from model manifests, never from here. Replaying the key with the same body returns the same study; with another body, 409.

Trial.title: Trial
Trial.description: One cross-validate step of a study: one candidate at one set of settings (TrialSpec, arch doc §11). Built from the comparison version and its run, never stored: its attempts are the run's attempts of that step (TrialAttempt), and its scores table is the TrialResult.

node_id.description: The cross-validate step in the comparison.

candidate.description: The shortlist alternative this trial scores.

settings.description: The searched settings this trial uses; empty for a model with nothing to search.

scores.description: Its per-fold scores table. Absent until it succeeds.

TrialState.description: Read from its attempts. not_started: none yet. running: one is in flight, or a retry is due. succeeded: one succeeded or reused a cached result. failed or cancelled: the run ended without a success.

StudyDetail.title: StudyDetail
StudyDetail.description: A study with its trials, in study order, and its run.

CreateWalk.title: CreateWalk
CreateWalk.description: Request for the engine to build, run and judge a flow from a question and its data (ADR-0060). Replaying the key with the same body returns the same walk; with another body, 409.

max_actions.description: Most actions (applies, runs, comparisons) the walk may take.

max_wall_seconds.description: Longest the walk may take, counted from its creation.

WalkSources.description: Local CSV or Parquet files, inside an allowed data folder, read as file_source steps. The first holds the rows to predict on; any other is joined to it by a rule.

Walk.title: Walk
Walk.description: The engine walking the methodology map for one question (ADR-0060). The one mutable control record: its status, head and stop change as it walks. What it did is its WalkSteps, which never change.

source_hashes.description: Each source's SHA-256 when the walk began, in the order of `sources`. Every round checks them: a source that changed stops the walk. Absent on walks made before they were recorded, and on one that stopped before building anything.

head_pipeline_version_id.description: The latest version the walk made. Absent when it stopped before building one.

stop.description: Why it stopped. Present once stopped.

WalkStatus.description: walking: it has more to do. stopped: it ended, for the reason in `stop`.

detail.description: What is open, for a person to read. Never parsed.

asks.description: Every question the walk's look found open, as one list (ADR-0063 amendment). Absent: the walk stopped for another reason.

WalkAsk.description: One open question. A method's ask names its method and options: a person answers it with one option, on the question. Any other names the question fact to state, as its key.

decides.description: The decision it holds back: a method's or a rule's key, such as data.repeated_items, or the question fact to state, such as question.success_bar.

method.description: The method that asks. Absent: a rule or the engine asks.

option.description: The option the method would take, once a person confirms it.

options.description: Every option of the method, for the person to pick from. Present exactly when method is.

WalkStopReason.description: complete: nothing is open. needs_person: only facts a person must state are open. limitation: a rule's recommended route reports a limit, such as no lift over the baseline. uncovered: an open item has no engine action yet. source_changed: a source file no longer holds what it held when the walk began. run_failed: the head's run failed and no rule can act on what it produced. stale: the head gained a version the walk did not make. budget_exhausted: the walk used its actions or its time. unverified: every rule is settled, but a promise a decision made did not pass on the head's run, so the test rows stay sealed. error: the engine could not take its next step; the detail says why.

WalkAction.description: build: made the first version from the question and sources. run: ran a version. apply: applied a rule's recommended alternative. compare: compared a Try's routes on fixed folds. measure: added or moved the steps that measure the evidence methods need, where each one attaches (ADR-0063). decide: a method chose an option, or applied a person's answer, and patched the flow by it. score: once every rule was settled, added one Evaluate on the test rows and ran it, once; no rule reads its score. verify: checked each promise the walk's decisions made, on the evidence the head's run measured (ADR-0063). stop: ended the walk.

WalkStep.title: WalkStep
WalkStep.description: One thing the engine did, and why (ADR-0060). Immutable; a walk's trail is its steps in round order.

round.description: Its place in the trail, from 0.

pipeline_version_id.description: The version it reviewed. Absent for build.

rule.description: The rule it acted for. Absent for build and run.

decides.description: What the rule decides. Absent for build, run and stop.

subject_node_id.description: The step the rule decided. Absent for build, run and stop.

made_pipeline_version_id.description: The version a build, apply, measure or decide made. Absent for a decide whose option changes no step.

effects.description: The patch a measure or decide step applied, in order (ADR-0063). Absent for every other action.

method.description: The method a decide step decided for.

option.description: The option a decide step took. A decide step always has method, decides, option and assurance.

assurance.description: How a decide step's option was taken.

bindings.description: The bindings a decide step's option made. Absent: none.

promises.description: The verifications a decide step's option promises, by name. Absent: none.

evidence.description: What a decide step's method read, whether it chose or a person answered. Absent: it read no evidence.

verifications.description: What a verify step found, one item per promise the walk's decisions made. Absent for every other action.

run_id.description: The run a run step started, or the run whose evidence a verify step read.

reason.description: Why, from the review item it acted on.

PromiseCheck.description: One promise checked on the evidence a run measured (ADR-0063).

promise.description: What holds when it passes, from method.yaml.

step.description: The step that measured the evidence. Absent when not_evaluated.

detail.description: What the evidence showed, or why nothing measured it.

PromiseResult.description: pass, fail, inconclusive: what verify_<name>() found. not_evaluated: no step measured the evidence it needs. Stale is never recorded: it is worked out against a newer version.

UsedEvidence.description: Evidence a method read: its kind, the step that measured it and the fields it saw (ADR-0064). Recorded with the decision, whether the method chose or a person answered its question, so a person can see what it rested on.

step.description: The producer step that measured it.

fields.description: The fields as the method saw them.

FlowDecisions.title: FlowDecisions
FlowDecisions.description: What decided a flow version, for people (ADR-0063 slice 5): the decisions of the walk that made the version or its nearest ancestor, each with the steps it shaped and the status of its promises on this version. Read only; worked out from the walk's steps.

walk_id.description: The walk that made the version or its nearest ancestor. Absent: no walk did, so nothing decided it.

name.description: The method's name, for the decision's title.

activity.description: The method's activity: one stage card, one notebook section.

reason.description: Why it was taken, from the decide step.

steps.description: The steps it shaped or rested on: those its patch changed, those its bindings read, those that measured its promises, and those that measured the evidence it read.

bindings.description: The bindings it made. Absent: none.

evidence.description: What the method read, with the step that measured it. Absent: none.

PromiseStatus.description: One promise's standing on the version asked about.

step.description: The step that measured its evidence. Absent when nothing did.

last_result.description: For stale: what the check found when it ran.

PromiseStanding.description: pass, fail, inconclusive, not_evaluated: what the last check found, and it still holds for this version. stale: the step that measured it, or a step before it, changed since; never shown as pass.

WalkDetail.title: WalkDetail
WalkDetail.description: A walk and its trail, oldest step first. A walk takes at most max_actions steps, so the trail is bounded.

WorkerMessage.title: WorkerMessage
WorkerMessage.description: Local worker protocol message (arch doc §11). Tagged by `type`.

Handshake.description: Worker → control plane, first message. Declares protocol version and operators the worker can run.

LeaseAttempt.description: Control plane → worker. Grants one attempt until lease_expires_at. Inputs are artifact references, never data.

code.description: The step's own code (ADR-0028): run this function instead of the operator's.

staging_uri.description: Only location the worker may write outputs to. Scoped to this attempt.

Heartbeat.description: Worker → control plane. Extends the lease.

Progress.description: Worker → control plane. Informational only; never authoritative.

ArtifactManifest.description: Worker → control plane. One output written to staging. The control plane verifies and commits it.

Complete.description: Worker → control plane. All manifests sent; attempt finished.

Fail.description: Worker → control plane. Attempt failed. failure_kind guides retry policy; side-effecting operators are never auto-retried.

Cancel.description: Control plane → worker. Stop the attempt.

Acknowledge.description: Control plane → worker. Last message for this attempt was committed.

InputBinding.description: Committed input artifact, resolved by the control plane. Read-only. The worker verifies content_hash before use.
